<h3 align="center">CASTAWAY <sub><i>(working title)</i></sub></h3>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours of one tiny island, one tall palm, one raft and one young woman in headphones.</b><br>
  She idles, nodding to the music. Every so often, something happens, and it waits for the beat to do it.<br>
  <i>Press any key. She will get round to it.</i>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <kbd>VIDEO</kbd> 16:9 · 1080p · 24 fps
  &nbsp;·&nbsp; <kbd>RUN</kbd> 10:00:00, seed 1992
  &nbsp;·&nbsp; <kbd>SOUND</kbd> synthesized, unheard
  &nbsp;·&nbsp; <kbd>SKY</kbd> daytime, always
</p>

A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams, and an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted in a sunny, hand-painted coastal anime style. [activities.toml](activities.toml) holds more than 90 activities, most of them on four timers, from small routines every few minutes (a coconut, a jog, some fishing) to "she could leave any time" once in a very long while. In between, a sea turtle drops by, a message in a bottle washes straight back, a coconut lands on a hermit crab and the crab walks off wearing it, and a shark in headphones nods along. Every activity starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat. Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py).

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

Live preview in the page, then export a YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes the frames and the server mixes in the sound. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. It is in development and no video has been published yet, so for now the loader is the only thing to watch, which is also, broadly, the plot.

The counts are the median of 200 simulated ten-hour runs, as the header of [activities.toml](activities.toml) says, and the activity count was 94 on 2026-10-01: 81 on the four timers and 13 chained follow-ups (it grows every few hours). Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and she is busy about a third of the time. Super-rare events are capped at three a run. `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates a run; the default is 10:00:00 with seed 1992, and the same seed makes the same video, event for event.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE MACHINERY</b>: the sound, the renderer and the tools</summary>

**The sound.** Everything is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far (181 on 2026-10-01). The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression over 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The ocean ambience is another seamless 60-second loop. The mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and the levels are adjustable for the master and per routine. It has been measured with great care and listened to by nobody, so this page will not tell you how it sounds. The loader above is silent, which seemed only fair.

**The picture.** The renderer is a web page, [web/index.html](web/index.html), served by [tools/serve.py](tools/serve.py): live preview, then a frame-exact export in the browser (WebCodecs H.264; in Chrome it measured 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30), after which the server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults. Around her, the scene has 26 entries of its own (4 always-on effects, 22 timed events): shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

**The tools.**

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `python tools/serve.py` | serves the renderer at http://127.0.0.1:8765/ and mixes the export |
| `python tools/schedule.py` | validates [activities.toml](activities.toml) and simulates a ten-hour run |
| `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` | the older Python reference renderer: a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display |
| `python tools/make_audio.py` | synthesizes every sound |

The working log, with every decision and what is still open, is [MUSING.md](MUSING.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>HOW THE LOADER WORKS</b>: palette rotation, a hammock made of a subtitle, and a scroll that steps</summary>

The banner borrows the look of the first graphical PC intros, from 1990 to 1993, when VGA mode 13h gave you 320 by 200 pixels and 256 colours picked from a palette: a framed metal plate, gradient bars, small magenta capitals on an arc, and one big scroller. It is drawn on that same 320-pixel-wide grid, and every colour is snapped to the VGA's 6 bits per channel, so the ramps band the way the real ones did.

**Palette rotation.** The diamonds behind the plate never move. Each ring is one of 16 palette entries, and the palette turns one step every sixteenth of a bar, so a band of light seems to travel outward while every pixel stays where it is. One turn takes 3 seconds, one bar of the theme. It is a stationary frame in which things appear to happen, which is the whole video in a 32-pixel tile.

**The hammock.** In the period loaders, an arc like this under the logo carried the group's full name. Here it carries the pitch, EVERY SO OFTEN, SOMETHING HAPPENS, hung from two rings under the plate, and she lies in it. Nothing else happens to her in the banner. She lifts her head on every beat and taps a foot, which is a fair summary of the other two thirds of the video. (The hammock is also a real activity in the schedule, on the rare timer. There, she ties one end to the palm, looks round for a second tree, finds none, and ties the other end to the raft. A metal plate is, if anything, an upgrade.)

**The choppy scroll.** Period scrollers stepped a few pixels at a time, and people noticed. This one moves exactly 4 pixels per step, 16 steps a second, which is also Castaway's own house rule: hard cuts and stepped movement. The text is followed by a copy of its own beginning, so the lap of about five minutes wraps without a seam. Everything else loops on the beat: the bars swing once every two bars of the theme, the glints wink every two bars, and the head and the foot go once a beat. With reduced motion switched on, it all holds still on the first frame, which already says CASTAWAY twice.

**Credits.** The style is modelled on early PC loaders by The Humble Guys, INC, USA and Fairlight, TRSI with The Dream Team, and Razor 1911 with Skillion. They are credited here as the reference only: none of their logos, letterforms or names appear in the banner, and IDLE HANDS is invented. The banner is an SVG built by a dependency-free Node script, with no text elements, no filters and no scripts.

</details>
